patterns.name: Trace function bootstrap for new threads
patterns.description: When the threading module has no hook for running code before a thread's main function, install a temporary trace function via threading.settrace() that on its first invocation removes itself (sys.settrace(None)), starts the real tracer, invokes it with the current event to avoid losing it, and returns the real trace function to continue tracing in that scope.
patterns.rationale: Python's threading module only supports running code before a thread's main function through the trace function hook. A self-removing bootstrap trace function is the only mechanism to jump-start per-thread tracer installation, ensuring every spawned thread gets a tracer without modifying user code.

patterns.name: Pause/resume stack for nested measurement scopes
patterns.description: A class-level list acts as a stack of active measurement collectors. When a new collector starts, the previous top is paused (its tracers stopped, threading.settrace set to None). When the new collector stops, it pops itself and resumes the one underneath. Only the innermost collector's tracers are active at any time.
patterns.rationale: Coverage measurement can be nested (e.g., a test suite starting its own Coverage inside an already-measured process). A pause/resume stack ensures only the innermost collector's tracers are active, preventing double-counting and trace function conflicts. Unlike thread-local stacks, this is a single global stack because sys.settrace is process-global.

patterns.name: Version-gated behavior flag class
patterns.description: A class with computed boolean class attributes that capture Python version-specific runtime behaviors (e.g., whether 'if __debug__' is optimized away, whether decorated defs get separate trace events, whether finally jumps back). These flags are computed once at module load time from version/implementation checks and used throughout the codebase to gate version-dependent logic.
patterns.rationale: Different Python versions and implementations (CPython, PyPy, Jython) have subtly different bytecode and tracing behaviors that affect coverage analysis. Rather than scattering version checks throughout the code, a single class of pre-computed boolean flags centralizes all version-dependent behavior decisions, making the version compatibility matrix explicit and testable.

occurrences.snippet:
class PYBEHAVIOR(object):
    """Flags indicating this Python's behavior."""
    pep626 = CPYTHON and (PYVERSION > (3, 10, 0, 'alpha', 4))
    optimize_if_debug = not pep626
    finally_jumps_back = ((3, 8) <= PYVERSION < (3, 10))
    trace_decorated_def = (PYVERSION >= (3, 8))
    nix_while_true = (PYVERSION >= (3, 8))
    omit_after_jump = pep626
    module_firstline_1 = pep626

patterns.name: Packed bitmap serialization for sparse integer sets
patterns.description: Sets of non-negative integers (line numbers) are serialized as packed bitmaps where bit i is set iff integer i is in the set. The bitmap is stored as a binary blob. Union and intersection operations work directly on the byte arrays with bitwise OR/AND. This provides compact storage for sparse integer sets and efficient set operations without deserialization.
patterns.rationale: Coverage data stores sets of executed line numbers per file per context. Individual row-per-line storage would be extremely verbose for files with hundreds of executed lines. A packed bitmap (numbits) stores N lines in ceil(max_line/8) bytes, and union operations (needed when combining data from multiple runs) are simple bitwise OR on byte arrays, avoiding full deserialization.

patterns.name: hasattr-based capability probing for dual C/Python implementation
patterns.description: When choosing between a C extension implementation and a pure Python fallback at runtime, the code probes the chosen implementation's capabilities using hasattr() checks on specific attribute names. The C implementation exposes more attributes (concur_id_func, file_tracers, check_include, disable_plugin) than the Python one. The setup code conditionally configures only the capabilities the chosen tracer supports, raising an error if a required capability is unavailable.
patterns.rationale: The C tracer (CTracer) supports features the Python tracer (PyTracer) does not: plugin-based file tracing, concurrency identifiers, and include checking. Rather than maintaining a separate capability registry or using ABCs, hasattr probes on the tracer instance directly discover which features are available. This keeps the Python tracer simple (no stub attributes) while allowing the C tracer to advertise its extra capabilities through attribute presence.

patterns.name: Config file fallback chain with owned-file vs piggyback distinction
patterns.description: Configuration files are tried in priority order (e.g., .coveragerc, setup.cfg, tox.ini, pyproject.toml). Files specifically for the tool ('owned files') are considered used even if empty. Files shared with other tools ('piggyback files') are only considered used if they contain tool-specific settings, distinguished by a section name prefix (e.g., 'coverage:' prefix in setup.cfg/tox.ini vs bare section names in owned files). The first used file wins; no merging across files.
patterns.rationale: Tools often piggyback on shared config files (setup.cfg, tox.ini) to avoid adding yet another config file. But these files may exist without containing any tool-specific settings. The owned-file vs piggyback distinction prevents treating an unrelated setup.cfg as the config source. The section prefix ('coverage:') namespaces tool settings within shared files, while owned files use bare section names. First-match-wins (rather than merge) keeps configuration predictable.

patterns.name: Defensive module copy to isolate from test mocking
patterns.description: At import time, create a shallow copy of a stdlib module (e.g., os) by instantiating a new ModuleType and copying all attributes. Subsequent code references the copy, not the original. This prevents test suites that mock stdlib functions (e.g., os.path.exists) from interfering with the framework's own internal use of those functions.
patterns.rationale: When a test suite mocks os.path.exists to test error handling, the framework's own code that calls os.path.exists would also be affected, causing spurious failures. By copying the module at import time and binding the copy to the module-level name, the framework operates on its own isolated copy that test mocking cannot reach. Submodules (e.g., os.path) are recursively isolated.

patterns.name: First-wins function composition for pluggable predicates
patterns.description: Multiple predicate functions (each taking the same argument and returning a value or None) are composed into a single function that calls them sequentially and returns the first non-None result. If all return None, the composed function returns None. The single-function case is optimized to return the function directly without wrapping.
patterns.rationale: When multiple plugins can each decide whether to start a new context, they need to be consulted in order until one claims responsibility. Rather than each call site iterating over the plugin list, a single composed function encapsulates the iteration logic. The first-wins semantics ensure only one plugin's context decision takes effect, and the short-circuit avoids calling unnecessary plugins.

patterns.name: Fork detection via pid checking for data safety
patterns.description: A data object stores the process id (pid) at initialization. Before any database operation, it compares the stored pid with the current pid. If they differ (indicating a fork), it resets all state (closes connections, clears caches) and chooses a new filename with a unique suffix, ensuring the forked child writes to its own data file rather than corrupting the parent's.
patterns.rationale: After os.fork(), the child process inherits the parent's open file handles and in-memory state, but SQLite connections are not fork-safe. By detecting the fork via pid mismatch and resetting state, the child gets a fresh data file with a unique suffix, preventing data corruption from concurrent writes to the same SQLite file. This is simpler and more portable than os.register_at_fork, which is only available on Python 3.7+.

patterns.name: Bare value object with function-based API for C/Python swapping
patterns.description: A value object class is intentionally defined as bare (just 'pass') with no methods. All behavior is implemented as module-level free functions that take the object as their first parameter. This allows both a C extension implementation and a pure Python implementation of the class to share the same function-based API without duplicating method logic or requiring inheritance.
patterns.rationale: When a value object needs to be instantiable in both C and Python, methods defined on the Python class would not be available on the C class (and vice versa). By keeping the class as a pure data container and implementing all operations as free functions, both implementations share identical operational code. The C class (CFileDisposition) only needs to provide the same attribute storage; the free functions work with either implementation.

occurrences.snippet:
class FileDisposition(object):
    """A simple value type for recording what to do with a file."""
    pass

# FileDisposition "methods": FileDisposition is a pure value object, so it can
# be implemented in either C or Python. Acting on them is done with these
# functions.

def disposition_init(cls, original_filename):
    disp = cls()
    disp.original_filename = original_filename
    disp.canonical_filename = original_filename
    disp.source_filename = None
    disp.trace = False
    disp.reason = ""
    disp.file_tracer = None
    disp.has_dynamic_filename = False
    return disp

patterns.name: Plugin permanent disable on exception
patterns.description: When a plugin raises an exception during its operation (e.g., file_tracer()), the plugin is permanently marked as disabled (_coverage_enabled = False) and skipped in all subsequent iterations. The exception is reported as a warning with a traceback, but the system continues operating without that plugin. A separate disable_plugin method handles runtime disablement from the tracer itself.
patterns.rationale: A faulty plugin that raises exceptions on every file would generate enormous noise and overhead if retried for each file. Permanently disabling the plugin after its first failure prevents cascading errors while allowing the rest of the system (including other plugins) to continue functioning. This is distinct from exception-to-warning degradation (which continues retrying) because it eliminates the error source entirely.

patterns.name: Comparison-key delegation for total ordering
patterns.description: A value object computes a single comparison-key tuple that encodes its domain's total order. A shared base class implements __hash__ and all six rich-comparison operators by delegating to that key (self._key <op> other._key), so native tuple comparison/hash yields correct ordering with no per-field comparison logic. Hot subclasses override the operators to inline a lazily-cached key for speed.
patterns.rationale: Centralizing the entire ordering in one precomputed key means equality, hashing, and sorting all derive from a single source of truth, and the base class defines the six operators once for any subclass that supplies _key. The key can encode non-obvious domain rules (e.g. PEP 440 trailing-zero collapse so 1.0.0 == 1, and pre/post/dev release ranks) as a flat tuple, turning each comparison into an O(1) tuple comparison instead of re-deriving semantics every time.

patterns.name: Restricted unpickler with class allowlist
patterns.description: A custom unpickler subclassing the pure-Python pickle._Unpickler overrides find_class() to reject any class not in a frozen allowlist of (module, name) tuples, blocking pickle's only arbitrary-code-execution vector. This makes pickle.load() safe for loading legacy/untrusted persisted state. The pure-Python _Unpickler base is required because the C-accelerated Unpickler bypasses find_class overrides on some runtimes (e.g. PyPy).
patterns.rationale: Persisted cookie jars may contain auth/session tokens and are loaded from disk, so loading must not execute arbitrary code. A restricted unpickler with an explicit class allowlist converts an unsafe pickle.load into a safe operation by intercepting global lookup, while still reading legacy binary pickle files for backward compatibility (JSON is preferred for new data).

patterns.name: Placeholder slot reservation for async resource creation
patterns.description: When acquiring a bounded async resource whose creation is itself async (a pooled connection), a lightweight placeholder object implementing the resource's interface (closed/transport/close/abort) is added to the 'acquired' set BEFORE awaiting creation. This reserves the capacity slot during the async gap so concurrent acquisitions cannot exceed the limit. After creation succeeds the placeholder is atomically swapped for the real protocol; on failure (or connector closure) the placeholder is released.
patterns.rationale: Checking a connection limit then awaiting _create_connection leaves a window where other tasks also pass the check and over-allocate. Reserving the slot with a placeholder before the await closes the race without holding a lock across the await; the swap-out happens with no awaits after it so cancellation cannot leak the real connection in the acquired set.

occurrences.snippet:
class _TransportPlaceholder:
    __slots__ = ("closed", "transport")
    def __init__(self, closed_future): self.closed = closed_future; self.transport = None
    def close(self) -> None: ...   # does nothing
    def abort(self) -> None: ...
# in connect():
placeholder = cast(ResponseHandler, _TransportPlaceholder(self._placeholder_future))
self._acquired.add(placeholder)            # reserve slot before async create
if self._limit_per_host: self._acquired_per_host[key].add(placeholder)
try:
    proto = await self._create_connection(req, traces, timeout)
except BaseException:
    self._release_acquired(key, placeholder); raise
# success: swap placeholder -> real protocol (no awaits after this)
self._acquired.remove(placeholder); self._acquired.add(proto)

patterns.name: Per-event-loop shared resource with weakref reference counting
patterns.description: A singleton manager shares an expensive per-loop resource (aiodns.DNSResolver) across many clients. It keeps a WeakKeyDictionary keyed by event loop mapping to (resource, WeakSet[client]), so resources are scoped per loop and the entry vanishes when the loop is GC'd. Each client registers into the loop's WeakSet; when the last client for a loop closes (WeakSet empties) the resource is cancelled and removed — reference counting driven entirely by object lifetimes, with no manual counters.
patterns.rationale: A native-async DNS resolver is bound to an event loop and costly to create, so all AsyncResolver instances on a loop should share one; but the manager must not outlive the loop or leak after every client closes. WeakKeyDictionary (per loop) + WeakSet (per client) yield automatic, race-free cleanup tied to GC lifetimes instead of explicit enter/exit refcounts, and custom-argument resolvers intentionally bypass sharing to get a dedicated instance.

patterns.name: Split-phase async context manager stack across lifecycle signals
patterns.description: A FrozenList of async-context-manager factories is entered eagerly on a startup signal (__aenter__ each, appending to an exits list) and exited in reverse order on a separate cleanup signal, collecting ALL errors into a single CleanupError. The enter and exit phases are decoupled — they run in different signal callbacks (on_startup / on_cleanup) rather than within one async-with block — and factories may be either real async CMs or plain async generators (auto-wrapped via asynccontextmanager).
patterns.rationale: App-scoped resources (DB pools, background tasks) must be set up at startup and torn down at cleanup, which are distinct signal-driven phases, not one synchronous scope. Splitting __aenter__/__aexit__ across signals while preserving LIFO teardown order and aggregating teardown errors (so one failing cleanup does not mask the rest) gives ExitStack-like guarantees across an asynchronous, signal-driven application lifecycle.

patterns.name: Decorator-collecting route table with deferred registration
patterns.description: A Sequence subclass exposes HTTP-method decorator methods (get/post/put/...) that each return a decorator appending an immutable RouteDef value object (frozen+slots attrs: method, path, handler, kwargs) to an internal list and returning the handler UNCHANGED. The table is router-agnostic; registration is deferred to a later bulk call where each RouteDef.register(router) dispatches to the matching router method by HTTP verb (add_get/add_post/... or add_route fallback).
patterns.rationale: Decoupling route declaration from the router lets routes be defined in any module without an Application/Router instance, composed, and registered in bulk later. Storing declarations as immutable value objects (not registration callbacks) makes the table introspectable and reusable across routers, while the decorator returns the handler unmodified so it remains independently callable/testable.

patterns.name: Lazy expiry min-heap with version-check dedup and amortized compaction
patterns.description: An expirable store maintains a min-heap of (expiry_time, key) ALONGSIDE a dict mapping key -> its current expiry. On each access, expired heap tops are popped and deleted only if their stored time equals the dict's current value for that key — stale heap entries (from keys re-set with a new expiry) are silently skipped. The heap is compacted (rebuilt from non-stale entries) only when it exceeds max(threshold, 2 x live-entry-count), amortizing rebuild cost.
patterns.rationale: Cookies can be re-set with a new max-age/expires, leaving superseded entries in the heap. A version check (heap time == dict time) distinguishes live from stale expirations without an O(n) rebuild on every update, so per-access expiry stays O(log n). Lazy compaction bounded by a minimum threshold keeps memory growth from accumulated stale entries in check without paying rebuild cost on small stores.

occurrences.snippet:
_MIN_SCHEDULED_COOKIE_EXPIRATION = 100
def _do_expiration(self):
    if (len(self._expire_heap) > _MIN_SCHEDULED_COOKIE_EXPIRATION
            and len(self._expire_heap) > len(self._expirations) * 2):
        self._expire_heap = [e for e in self._expire_heap if self._expirations.get(e[1]) == e[0]]  # drop stale
        heapq.heapify(self._expire_heap)
    now = time.time()
    while self._expire_heap:
        when, cookie_key = self._expire_heap[0]
        if when > now: break
        heapq.heappop(self._expire_heap)
        if self._expirations.get(cookie_key) == when: ...   # version check: only delete live expiry
def _expire_cookie(self, when, domain, path, name):
    if self._expirations.get(cookie_key) == when: return   # dedup: skip duplicate push

patterns.name: Recursive content-type-dispatched async reader over shared stream
patterns.description: A multipart body parser is an async iterator whose next() delimits a part by scanning for a boundary over a single shared StreamReader, reads that part's headers, then dispatches by Content-Type: multipart/* subtypes yield a NESTED instance of the same reader class (multipart_reader_cls=None -> type(self)), enabling arbitrary nesting depth; other types yield a leaf BodyPartReader. Both the nested-reader and part-reader classes are overridable class attributes. All nesting levels read from the one underlying stream in sequence, with boundary bytes pushed back (unread_data) so the next reader resumes at the correct position.
patterns.rationale: Multipart bodies can nest (multipart/mixed inside multipart/form-data). Making the reader recursively self-dispatch by content type, with the reader class overridable as a class attribute, handles arbitrary nesting uniformly without per-level special cases. Async iteration over a shared stream (rather than a sans-IO feed) lets each part be consumed lazily and back-pressured, and pushback of boundary bytes lets sibling/nested readers share one stream cleanly.
